messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak landed yesterday we're seeing a consistent ~6-8% P50 latency regression on staging for Mixtral-8x workloads. Brief profile attached, can people +1 if they see this locally?

maya: acked. any idea which selector path is being chosen? small-seq vs long-seq?

alex: It looks like for short sequences (<128) the selector picks the fused-attn kernel variant that we pushed (optimizes for throughput). But the profiler shows extra memcpy + cast overhead around KV-cache handling. snippet:```
GPU memcpy H2D: 1.2ms
KV cast FP16->FP8 (host): 0.8ms
kernel fused-attn: 0.9ms
old kernel (non-fused): 1.1ms
```
So net latency is worse despite the faster kernel because of cache precision conversions.

chris: interesting — are we converting the prefix-cache at enqueue time or at serve time? that matters a lot.

alex: current code converts on serve (right before forming KV tensors) to support mixed caches (some customers on BF16, some on FP16). leads to per-request copies.

sam: that matches what i saw in a repro. conversion is happening inside the request loop which prevents batching from folding conversions. we should try conversion-on-write (normalize cache to canonical format when inserting) so read path is cheap.

maya: +1 to normalize-on-write. also want to flag RoPE scaling behavior for Mixtral/llama variants — we saw greater KV sensitivity when head_dim != kv_dim. RoPE scaling mismatch triggers extra reformatting in the runtime.

chris: model-specific notes:
- Llama2 70B: stable with BF16 KV, lower quantization tolerance.
- Mistral-7B: tolerates FP8-ish KV quantization but needs per-head calibration.
- Mixtral-8x: head_dim/kv_dim mismatch = more cache expansions; avoid dynamic reshape on hot path.
- Qwen-series: uses rotary that is less sensitive to low-precision cache but has larger kv dims -> bigger memory pressure.

alex: profiling run from perf-bot (nightly) also flagged higher GPU occupancy due to smaller, more frequent kernels (lots of casts). perf-bot output:```
perf-bot: nightly-run (mixtral-8x): p50 81ms (baseline 76ms)
hotspots:
  - memcpy H2D: 14%
  - kv_cast_host: 10%
  - kernel_launch overhead: 8%
```

maya: hypothesis: FP8/quantized KV reduces memory but increases CPU-side packing/unpacking and kernel-launch count. For mixes we should evaluate: canonicalize KV to BF16 on write, keep on-device in BF16, and only quantize to FP8 when spilling to tiered cache (SSD) or migrating to cold region.

sam: +1. Also propose eviction policy tweak: current LRU evicts by token age which is bad for prefix-heavy chat sessions. Suggest prefix-aware weighted eviction: keep recent tokens from active prefixes pinned. cheap heuristic: pin first N tokens per session ID.

chris: batching heuristics: reduce conversion work by moving conversion outside batch boundary. i.e. pre-batch normalization -> aggregate conversions once per batch instead of per-request. tweak: increase max_batch_delay from 2ms to 6ms for short-seq flows — should improve amortization. but we need to watch p99.

alex: action items:
- maya: implement normalize-on-write for KV caches (BF16 canonical) and add migration path for FP8 spill. (owner: maya)
- sam: prototype prefix-aware eviction + unit tests (owner: sam)
- chris: batching change + conversion-on-batch, run canary on staging with Mixtral/Llama/Mistral traces (owner: chris)
- perf-bot: schedule 12h nightly run comparing baseline vs branch w/ these changes (owner: perf-bot)

maya: quick patch idea for normalize-on-write:```python
# on cache insert
def insert_kv(session_id, kv_tensor, precision):
    if precision != BF16:
        kv_tensor = cast_to_bf16(kv_tensor)  # one-time cost
    store_device_kv(session_id, kv_tensor)
```
This avoids host-side casts on read.

sam: for eviction: start with simple pin-first-N + LRU elsewhere. we'll measure memory delta.

alex: can we also add a lightweight perf counter for "kv-conversion-time" so we can see conversion cost per request in live traces?

perf-bot: done — added kv_conversion_ms histogram to nightly tracing.

chris: one more: RoPE scaling impacts — when we change RoPE scale we re-run positional multipliers per head, avoid per-token recompute by caching rotated coeffs per head_dim. small memory cost, big CPU win.

maya: agreed — cache rotary coefficients keyed by (model_id, head_dim, rope_scale) on device. flush on model reload.

alex: cool. let's land small patches in this order: normalize-on-write -> batching conversion -> eviction. I'll coordinate canary windows. thanks all :thumbsup:
